# Startup files {.dark-slide background-color="#111C26"}

[BLOCK 2 &middot; PART A]{.eyebrow}

::: {.accent-bar}
:::

[Which files R reads at startup, and in what order.]{.subhead}

## Environment files vs profile files

### Environment files

`Renviron`-style: lines of `NAME=value`, with `${VAR-default}` expansion.
Not R code. Use for repository URLs, library paths, proxy settings.

### Profile files

`Rprofile`-style: R code, sourced into the global environment. Use for
`options()`, `.Library.site`, `.First()`, anything needing logic.

::: {.note}
[Only `base` is loaded]{.note-label}
When profile files are sourced, only `base` is loaded. Write
`utils::install.packages()`, not `install.packages()`
([`?Startup`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/Startup.html)).
:::

## Startup order

```text
1.  $(R RHOME)/etc/Renviron       <- always; set by configure; DO NOT EDIT
2.  $R_ENVIRON      else  $(R RHOME)/etc/Renviron.site
3.  $R_ENVIRON_USER else  ./.Renviron  else  ~/.Renviron      <- first hit only
4.  $R_PROFILE      else  $(R RHOME)/etc/Rprofile.site
5.  $R_PROFILE_USER else  ./.Rprofile  else  ~/.Rprofile      <- first hit only
6.  .RData          (unless --no-restore-data)
7.  .First()        (if defined)
8.  .First.sys()    -> attaches options("defaultPackages")
```

All environment files are read before any profile file. A profile can use a
variable from `Renviron.site`, not the other way round
([`?Startup`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/Startup.html)).

## `R_ENVIRON` and `R_ENVIRON_USER`

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

Create a site and a user environment file in the container:

```bash
mkdir -p /startup/home /startup/project && cd /startup
cat > site.Renviron <<'EOF'
# Site environment file: read first, R_ENVIRON points here
MY_TEAM=site
MY_REPO=${MY_REPO-'https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest'}
EOF

cat > user.Renviron <<'EOF'
# User environment file: read after the site file, R_ENVIRON_USER points here
MY_TEAM=user
EOF
```

```bash
R_ENVIRON=site.Renviron R -q --no-echo -e 'Sys.getenv("MY_TEAM")'

R_ENVIRON=site.Renviron R_ENVIRON_USER=user.Renviron \
  R -q --no-echo -e 'Sys.getenv("MY_TEAM")'
```

`R_ENVIRON` and `R_ENVIRON_USER` point R at a file. Both files set `MY_TEAM`; the user
file is read after the site file, so its value wins.

## `$(R RHOME)/etc/Renviron` is generated by `configure`

Do not modify it. Put site settings in `Renviron.site`, which is read later
and overrides it.

```bash
# read this, do not edit it
grep -E '^(R_LIBS_SITE|R_LIBS_USER)' /usr/lib/R/etc/Renviron
```

```text
R_LIBS_USER=${R_LIBS_USER:-'%U'}
R_LIBS_SITE=${R_LIBS_SITE:-'/usr/local/lib/R/site-library:%S'}
```

## `./.Renviron` replaces `~/.Renviron`

Only the first user environment file is read: a project's `./.Renviron`
replaces `~/.Renviron`; it does not add to it.

```bash
cat > home/.Renviron <<'EOF'
MY_TEAM=home
EOF

R -q --no-echo -e 'path.expand("~")'
HOME=/startup/home R -q --no-echo -e 'path.expand("~")'
HOME=/startup/home R -q --no-echo -e 'Sys.getenv(c("MY_TEAM", "MY_PROJECT"))'
```

```bash
cat > project/.Renviron <<'EOF'
MY_PROJECT=yes
EOF

cd project
HOME=/startup/home R -q --no-echo -e 'Sys.getenv(c("MY_TEAM", "MY_PROJECT"))'
cd ..
```

In `project/`, R finds `./.Renviron` and never reads `~/.Renviron`.

## Path codes in `Renviron`

R expands these, not the shell
([`?.libPaths`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/libPaths.html)).
Debian puts `/usr/local/lib/R/site-library` in front of R's default site
library, `%S`.

| Code | Expands to |
|---|---|
| `%V` | R version with patch level, `4.6.1` |
| `%v` | R version without patch level, `4.6` |
| `%p` | Platform, `x86_64-pc-linux-gnu` |
| `%a` | Architecture |
| `%o` | OS |
| `%U` | R's default `R_LIBS_USER` |
| `%S` | R's default `R_LIBS_SITE` |

```bash
R -q --no-echo -e 'Sys.getenv("R_LIBS_USER")'
```

```text
[1] "/root/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.6"
```

The version and platform in the path keep a user's 4.5 and 4.6 packages
apart.

## Overridable defaults with `${VAR-default}`

A site can ship a default that a user can still override
([`?Startup`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/Startup.html)).

| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `${FOO-bar}` | `FOO` if set, otherwise `bar` |
| `${FOO:-bar}` | `FOO` if set *and non-empty*, otherwise `bar` |
| `${FOO}` | `FOO` if set, otherwise `""` |
| `$FOO` | Not expanded. The braces are required. |

Use the same form in your own `Renviron.site`.

## `${VAR-default}` in practice

`site.Renviron` sets `MY_REPO=${MY_REPO-'…/cran/latest'}`.

```bash
R_ENVIRON=site.Renviron R -q --no-echo -e 'Sys.getenv("MY_REPO")'

MY_REPO=https://example.org/repo R_ENVIRON=site.Renviron \
  R -q --no-echo -e 'Sys.getenv("MY_REPO")'
```

When `MY_REPO` is already set, the file's default is not used.

## Writing `Renviron.site` and `Rprofile.site`

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

```bash
cat >> /usr/lib/R/etc/Renviron.site <<'EOF'
# Where our packages come from, overridable per user
R_PKG_REPO=${R_PKG_REPO-'https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest'}
EOF

cat >> /usr/lib/R/etc/Rprofile.site <<'EOF'
local({
  options(repos = c(CRAN = Sys.getenv("R_PKG_REPO")))
  options(Ncpus = max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L))
  options(warn = 1)
})
EOF
```


## Check which file set it

```bash
R -q --no-echo -e 'print(getOption("repos")); print(getOption("Ncpus"))'
```

```text
                                          CRAN
"https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest"
[1] 13
```

`--vanilla` skips the site and user startup files:

```bash
R --vanilla -q --no-echo -e 'print(getOption("repos"))'
```

```text
         CRAN
"@CRAN@"
```

`"@CRAN@"` means no repository is set: `install.packages()` asks for a
mirror, and fails in a non-interactive session.

## Wrap site profile code in `local()`

```r
# Leaks `x` into every user's global environment
x <- 3
options(width = x)

# Correct
local({
  x <- 3
  options(width = x)
})
```

Profile code runs in the global environment, so top-level assignments show
up in every user's workspace. The exceptions are `.Library.site`, `.First`,
and `.Last`
([`?Startup`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/Startup.html)).

## Top-level assignments leak into the workspace

```bash
cat > leak.Rprofile <<'EOF'
x <- 42
EOF

R_PROFILE_USER=leak.Rprofile R -q --no-echo -e 'ls()'
```

A top-level assignment in a profile shows up in the workspace.


## Only `base` is attached while profiles run

```bash
cat > utils.Rprofile <<'EOF'
print(head(letters, 3))
EOF

R_PROFILE_USER=utils.Rprofile R -q --no-echo -e '1'
```

```bash
cat > fixed-utils.Rprofile <<'EOF'
print(utils::head(letters, 3))
EOF

R_PROFILE_USER=fixed-utils.Rprofile R -q --no-echo -e '1'
```

`head()` is in `utils`, which is not attached yet. `utils::head()` works.

## What belongs in `Rprofile.site`

| Setting | Why |
|---|---|
| `options(repos = ...)` | `install.packages()` works without a mirror prompt |
| `.Library.site <- ...` | Sets the site library; users cannot change it afterwards. `R_LIBS_SITE` is the overridable alternative |
| `options(Ncpus = ...)` | Installs source packages in parallel |
| `options(warn = 1)` | Warnings print when they occur, not at the end |
| `options(timeout = 300)` | The default of 60 seconds is often too short for large files |

Sources: [`?options`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/options.html),
[R-admin](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html#Managing-libraries),
[`?download.file`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/download.file.html).

## Linux binaries from Package Manager

Package Manager has two URL forms for Linux binaries
([Package Manager docs](https://docs.posit.co/rspm/admin/serving-binaries.html)):

```text
https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/noble/latest
https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest/bin/linux/noble-x86_64/4.6
```

- **`__linux__/<distro>`** picks the R version and architecture from R's
  user agent. R's default works with the `libcurl` download method; other
  setups may need `options(HTTPUserAgent = ...)`. The docs include a
  diagnostic script.
- **`bin/linux/<distro>-<arch>/<r-version>`** puts everything in the URL and
  needs no configuration.

## Bisect startup problems with flags

```bash
R --vanilla -q -e 'getOption("repos")'        # 1. is it configuration at all?
R --no-init-file -q -e 'getOption("repos")'   # 2. not the user profile
R --no-site-file -q -e 'getOption("repos")'   # 3. not the site profile
R --no-environ -q -e 'Sys.getenv("R_LIBS_SITE")'  # 4. not an environment file
```

Inside a broken session, check whether something redirects the user files:

```r
Sys.getenv("R_PROFILE_USER")
Sys.getenv("R_ENVIRON_USER")
```
